headline: The Pentagon is trying to speed up buying of AI for military targeting, using five-minute company videos.
score_reason: Pool score 7 kept: the full article was read and matches the headline.
importance_line: What changed: a fast-track route lets the Pentagon award AI deals in under a week in some cases, with less competition, and such deals can reach $500 million without notice to Congress. Companies that use it get a quicker path to military contracts, and the oversight concerns raised by Senator Joni Ernst of Iowa are not yet answered.
summary: WIRED reports that the Pentagon's Tradewinds program, run by its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office, gives 'post-competitive' status, meaning buyers can skip some competition rules, to AI companies whose five-minute videos are accepted. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are listed as participants, but none confirmed whether Tradewinds was used for the deals WIRED identified, and Senator Joni Ernst of Iowa warns of weak oversight.
